notes:
- The launch screen usually does not draw at all: Opening the app read the stored theme, the interface settings and the app-lock choice, drew a placeholder until they answered, and only then read the stored session and the first-run answer behind a second placeholder - and only then did the dashboard start reading your saved list off disk. None of those reads depends on the one above it; they were serialised purely by the order the screens were composed in. They all start together at process start now, and the answers they produce seed the screens that used to draw a placeholder waiting for them, so a launch reads once, concurrently, and the first frame is the app.
- Your list's saved copy is parsed before the first frame: The dashboard's first paint waits on two saved records - your profile and your list - and the list is the one snapshot measured in megabytes. That file read used to begin after both splash screens had resolved, so the reader watched a skeleton while a large file was read and parsed. It is started with everything else now, while the window is still being inflated.
- A custom display density no longer resizes the app on launch: The display density is applied to the whole app above the theme, and the launch screen only waited for the theme and the lock - so a first frame drawn at the shipped default was re-laid-out a frame later at the reader's chosen density. The density is now part of what the launch wait covers, and an unreadable interface file falls back to the shipped defaults instead of holding the splash until the watchdog.
- A title page's blurred backdrop is decoded at the blur's resolution: The artwork behind the Info page was decoded at the panel's own resolution - about 10 MB on a 1080p phone, twice while the cover crossfaded to the banner - for a picture drawn under an 18dp blur and a legibility scrim. It decodes at half that width on Soft and a third on Heavy: four and nine times less bitmap to allocate, decode and upload, and it competes far less with the poster cache on the list behind it. Crisp, which is the setting that means a sharp picture, keeps the full decode, and the hero is untouched.

Build 688.
